target.title: fix(anthropic): preserve Retry-After header from transport error responses for auto-retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103849. When the Anthropic Messages transport receives an HTTP 429 rate-limit error with a `Retry-After` header (e.g. `Retry-After: 30`), the header value is discarded. The error is turned into a plain `Error` carrying only the response body text. Downstream, `AgentSession.prepareRetry` falls back to fixed 2s/4s/8s exponential backoff, so all retries land inside the still-active server cooldown window and the turn fails outright instead of succeeding after the server's actual cooldown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three coordinated changes, each at its correct ownership boundary:

1. **`createAnthropicMessagesClient`** (`src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`) — parses the `Retry-After` HTTP header on non-OK responses and attaches `status` (number) and `retryAfterSeconds` (number) to the thrown `Error`.

2. **`extractTransportErrorDetails`** (`src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`) — reads `status` and `retryAfterSeconds` from enriched error objects and returns them in `TransportErrorDetails`, which `Object.assign` propagates onto the `AssistantMessage` via `assignTransportErrorDetails`.

3. **`prepareRetry`** (`src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`) — when the `AssistantMessage` carries a `retryAfterSeconds` value, uses `Math.max(exponentialDelayMs, retryAfterMs)` instead of purely exponential backoff, so retries wait at least as long as the server requests.

`AssistantMessage` type (`packages/llm-core/src/types.ts`) gains optional `status?: number` and `retryAfterSeconds?: number` fields, consistent with the existing `errorCode`/`errorType`/`errorBody` error metadata pattern.

The existing `parseRetryAfterSeconds` in `provider-transport-fetch.ts` is already correct but only feeds the `x-should-retry` SDK path. A lightweight inline `parseRetryAfterHeaderSeconds` was added closer to the non-SDK client site to keep module dependency boundaries clean.

## User Impact

Users with `anthropic-messages` providers (direct Anthropic API, proxy/third-party gateways returning `Retry-After` headers) now get auto-retry that respects the server's actual cooldown window. When the server sends `Retry-After: 30`, retries wait at least 30 seconds before re-attempting instead of hammering with 2s/4s/8s backoff.

No behavior change for transports that do not attach `retryAfterSeconds` to errors — those continue with the existing exponential backoff. No behavior change for successful (200) responses.

## Evidence

- **TypeScript**: `pnpm tsgo:core` — passes
- **Tests**:
  - `transport-stream-shared.test.ts`: 12/12 ✓ (2 new: `status`/`retryAfterSeconds` extraction from enriched errors, graceful absence on plain errors)
  - `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`: 108/108 ✓ (1 new: HTTP 429 + `Retry-After: 30` → error carries `status: 429`, `retryAfterSeconds: 30`)
  - `provider-transport-fetch.test.ts`: 94/94 ✓
  - `retry.test.ts`: 21/21 ✓
  - `embedded-agent-runner/helpers.test.ts`: 16/16 ✓
  - `session/settings-manager.test.ts`: 3/3 ✓
  Fixes #103849

target.title: fix(tasks): reconcile CLI subagent cancellation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This is a narrow cancellation-path follow-up for TaskFlow rows that already have a tracked child relationship but do not get fully reconciled today.

In local upgrade-replay incidents, operator cancellation could fail to clear active task state or could clear only the registry row while leaving a backing child session alive:

- stale subagent wrapper rows could return `Subagent was not running.` and stay non-terminal, blocking flow cancellation with `One or more child tasks are still active.`
- `runtime=cli` task rows whose `childSessionKey` points at a `:subagent:` child could be marked cancelled without killing the backing child session, allowing the child to continue appending events or reappear after restart

This PR keeps the fix at the operator cancellation entrypoint. It does not replace #90505, which is a broader maintenance-side reconciliation fix for killed subagent task rows and carries a separate session-state transition/docs tradeoff.

## Summary

- cancel CLI-tracked tasks with `childSessionKey` pointing at a `:subagent:` child by killing the backing subagent session before marking the registry row cancelled
- preserve backing subagent terminal/finalizing outcomes before cancelling CLI mirror rows, so a late `succeeded`/`failed`/finalizing state is not overwritten by operator cancellation
- keep direct/main CLI follow-up rows registry-only so cancelling them does not kill the user's main session
- allow found-but-not-running subagent wrappers to fall through to registry cancellation instead of returning `Subagent was not running.`
- keep childless ACP `context_engine_turn_maintenance` rows non-cancellable without an owner handoff, because active deferred maintenance rows need an owner-aware cancellation path

## Relationship to existing work

Related issue: #90444.

This is a narrow follow-up to the uncovered operator-facing cancellation cases described in #90444. It intentionally does not change the broader maintenance reconciliation model covered by #90505.

#90505 remains the larger active/candidate fix for killed subagent task-row finalization. This PR only addresses cancellation entrypoints that can otherwise leave TaskFlow rows or backing child sessions inconsistent even when an operator explicitly tries to repair the state with `tasks cancel` / `tasks flow cancel`.

## Evidence

Local production/operator evidence, sanitized:

- `openclaw tasks cancel` returned `Subagent was not running.` for a found-but-stopped subagent wrapper, but the task row stayed non-terminal and continued blocking flow cancellation.
- A `runtime=cli` task with a `:subagent:` child session was marked cancelled in the task registry without stopping the backing child session; after restart/restore, the child could continue producing events and the task could effectively reappear as running.
- After applying the CLI/subagent cancellation-path behavior locally, restarting the gateway, and replaying the affected cleanup, `running=0`, `queued=0`, and task audit no longer reported stale running/queued/cancel-stuck rows for these cases.

Focused validation on this branch:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.test.ts`
  - `src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts`: `Tests 113 passed (113)`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.test.ts`: `Tests 21 passed (21)`
- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/tasks/task-registry.ts src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/context-engine-maintenance.test.ts`

## Negative Boundaries

- Does not change the `lost -> succeeded` maintenance reconciliation rule discussed in #90505.
- Does not attempt to solve the larger session write-lock / session-state design line.
- Does not kill direct/main CLI child sessions; those remain registry-only cancellation to avoid terminating the user's main conversation.
- Does not overwrite backing subagent terminal/finalizing outcomes when a CLI mirror row cancellation races with completion.
- Does not mark childless `acp/context_engine_turn_maintenance` rows cancelled without an owner-aware cancellation handoff; stale maintenance cleanup should be handled by a separate owner-aware follow-up.

target.title: fix(tavily): fall back to process.env when config SecretRef is unresolvable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`tavily_search` and `tavily_extract` fail at runtime with `unresolved SecretRef "env:default:TAVILY_API_KEY"` even when `TAVILY_API_KEY` is set in the gateway process environment. The configured `SecretRef` points at an env-backed credential that the active runtime snapshot can't inline-resolve, but the plugin's own call chain already has a `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` fallback — the helper in strict mode throws before that fallback can run. Bundled peers (`brave`, `firecrawl`, `exa`) use `readConfiguredSecretString` from `extensions/web-search-provider-common` and don't hit this; tavily and exa are the only remaining `extensions/*/src/config.ts` helpers still throwing in strict mode.

## Evidence

**Environment:** Linux, Node v24, OpenClaw `v2026.6.8` (commit `8a24f93`), with the patch applied via `prestart.sh` step 7/7 in the contributor's runtime overlay.

**Reproduction (before fix):**

```bash
export TAVILY_API_KEY=***
openclaw config set plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey \
  --ref-provider default --ref-source env --ref-id TAVILY_API_KEY
openclaw infer web search --provider tavily --query ping --limit 1 --json
# → Error: plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey: unresolved SecretRef "env:default:TAVILY_API_KEY". Resolve this command against an active gateway runtime snapshot before reading it.
```

**After this patch:** Same command reaches Tavily. With a dummy key, the expected downstream error is `401 Unauthorized: missing or invalid API key` (auth failure, not SecretRef failure). With a live key, the call returns search results.

## Real behavior proof — captured runtime logs (2026-06-21)

Real LLM-driven MCP tool calls captured from the contributor's gateway log
on 2026-06-21, when an agent tried a research query about Tailscale and
the MCP `tavily_search` / `tavily_extract` tools failed for the same
reason. These are the exact log lines:

```
2026-06-21T12:05:16.462+00:00 [tools] tavily_search failed: plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey: unresolved SecretRef "env:default:TAVILY_API_KEY". Resolve this command against an active gateway runtime snapshot before reading it. raw_params={"query":"Tailscale pricing 2026 Personal Pro Enterprise plans devices users","max_results":8,"include_answer":true}
2026-06-21T12:05:16.549+00:00 [tools] tavily_search failed: plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey: unresolved SecretRef "env:default:TAVILY_API_KEY". Resolve this command against an active gateway runtime snapshot before reading it. raw_params={"query":"Tailscale features MagicDNS HTTPS TLS certificates HTTPS Let's Encrypt 2025","max_results":8,"include_answer":true}
2026-06-21T12:05:16.553+00:00 [tools] tavily_search failed: plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey: unresolved SecretRef "env:default:TAVILY_API_KEY". Resolve this command against an active gateway runtime snapshot before reading it. raw_params={"query":"Tailscale Kubernetes operator k3s integration GitOps GitHub","max_results":6}
2026-06-21T12:05:29.366+00:00 [tools] tavily_extract failed: plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey: unresolved SecretRef "env:default:TAVILY_API_KEY". Resolve this command against an active gateway runtime snapshot before reading it. raw_params={"urls":["https://tailscale.com/","https://tailscale.com/kb/"],"query":"Tailscale documentation features overview","chunks_per_source":3}
```

Same symptom, four independent calls within a 13-second window — the
fallback to `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` was being skipped because the
resolver threw in strict mode. With this PR applied on the same runtime,
the same agent's research turn completed and the Tailscale sources were
ingested normally.

## Current-installation runtime proof (2026-06-27, this very instance)

The contributor's active OpenClaw container is running OpenClaw `v2026.6.10`
with the bundled `tavily-plugin v2026.6.8` patched in-place by
`prestart.sh` step 7/7 (so the runtime resolver carries the same
inspect-mode + allowlist behavior this PR introduces for upstream). To
confirm the patched Tavily plugin path is reachable from this very
instance, Aiko (the contributor's assistant) invoked the MCP `tavily_search`
tool on 2026-06-27T01:36:30Z with the query `OpenClaw 2026.6.10 release
notes tavily plugin`. The call returned three real Tavily results in
1213 ms with no `UnresolvedSecretInputError` and no `unresolved SecretRef`
message. The companion gateway-side line from
`/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-06-27.log` (subsystem `gateway/ws`) shows
the prerequisite step succeeded cleanly:

```
2026-06-27T01:36:14.935+00:00 [gateway/ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.resolve 93ms conn=94febf43…1322 id=efb0b53a…cc65
```

That `secrets.resolve 93ms` line is the gateway resolving
`plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey` for the active call —
the same path that the contributor's runtime fix in `prestart.sh` and the
upstream PR both keep non-throwing. The runtime error observed in the
2026-06-21 logs above is not reproducible here.

## Exact-head runtime proof (2026-06-28)

Built and tested from the exact PR head commit in an isolated Docker container (no prestart.sh, no patched runtime overlay).

**Environment:**
- Image: `docker.io/library/node:24-bookworm-slim` (Node v24.18.0, pnpm 11.2.2)
- Platform: linux/amd64
- Branch: `fix/tavily-secretref-fallback`
- Commit: `3a9963a2bf69a0831c198361c04a68128ca3ef66`
- Source cloned from: `git@github.com:kzzalews/openclaw-upstream.git` (depth=1, branch only)

**Step 1 — Source inspection (key lines from `extensions/tavily/src/config.ts` at head):**

```
3:import { canResolveEnvSecretRefInReadOnlyPath } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/extension-shared";
48:function resolveConfiguredSecret(
57:    mode: "inspect",
74:    !canResolveEnvSecretRefInReadOnlyPath({
88:  const resolved = resolveConfiguredSecret(
```

**Step 2 — Unit tests (exact-head, Node 24, pnpm 11.2.2):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-misc.config.ts \
    extensions/tavily/src/config.test.ts

    Start at  19:23:56
    Duration  844ms (transform 413ms, setup 236ms, import 392ms, tests 56ms, environment 0ms)
```

All 8 cases pass (production SDK resolver path, no `vi.mock`).

**Step 3 — End-to-end runtime proof (configured env SecretRef → Tavily 401):**

Input scenario: `plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey` is an env SecretRef
(`{source: "env", provider: "default", id: "TAVILY_API_KEY"}`) — the exact configuration
that caused `UnresolvedSecretInputError` before this PR. The runtime snapshot cannot
inline-resolve it.

```
$ node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.cjs proof-runtime.mts

=== PR #95110 exact-head runtime proof ===
commit: 3a9963a2bf69a0831c198361c04a68128ca3ef66
branch: fix/tavily-secretref-fallback
timestamp: 2026-06-28T19:23:58.869Z

Input: configured env SecretRef {source:'env', provider:'default', id:'TAVILY_API_KEY'}
Env:   TAVILY_API_KEY = tvly-proof-dummy-3a9963a2bf69

resolveTavilyApiKey() returned: "tvly-proof-dummy-3a9963a2bf69"
  → Key resolved from process.env fallback (not thrown): OK

Making HTTP call to api.tavily.com with resolved key...
HTTP status: 401 Unauthorized
Response: {"detail":{"error":"Unauthorized: missing or invalid API key."}}

✓ PROOF COMPLETE: configured env SecretRef fallback passed key to Tavily

```

The key (`tvly-proof-dummy-3a9963a2bf69`) is a redacted dummy — the `401 Unauthorized`
response from `api.tavily.com` confirms the key reached the Tavily endpoint. With a live
key, the same call returns real search results instead of auth failure.

## Test coverage

`extensions/tavily/src/config.test.ts` covers the new `resolveConfiguredSecret`
helper end-to-end against the bundled SDK (no `vi.mock` — production
resolver path runs against `resolveSecretInputString` with `mode: "inspect"`
and `canResolveEnvSecretRefInReadOnlyPath`):

- returns the configured string `apiKey` as-is (happy path)
- falls back to `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` when the configured env SecretRef is unresolvable AND its id is `TAVILY_API_KEY`
- trims whitespace from the configured env SecretRef id before matching (`"  TAVILY_API_KEY  "` still falls through)
- does **NOT** fall back when the configured SecretRef is a `file` source
- does **NOT** fall back when the configured SecretRef is an `exec` source
- does **NOT** fall back when the configured env SecretRef targets a different env var
- does **NOT** fall back when the configured env SecretRef uses a provider not in `cfg.secrets.providers` allowlist
- returns `undefined` when neither config nor env var is set

Run with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-misc.config.ts extensions/tavily/src/config.test.ts`. All 8 cases pass.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] Integrations (tavily web-search plugin)

## Linked Issue

Fixes a regression where the bundled tavily plugin (added in PR #49200) cannot fall back to `TAVILY_API_KEY` when the configured `plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey` is a SecretRef the active runtime snapshot doesn't inline-resolve. Related closed issues that did not catch this runtime-side gap:

- #76491 — closed as "implemented on current main", but the vendored tavily/exa helpers (`extensions/tavily/src/config.ts`, `extensions/exa/src/config.ts`) still throw in strict mode.
- #82621 — closed by PR #82798 for the CLI `infer web search` path; this PR fixes the runtime plugin path that #82798 left open.

Related: #95112 by @liuhao1024 — closed unmerged (uses the same `mode: "inspect"` core, without the file/exec/non-matching-env allowlist added here). If maintainers prefer that approach, the inspect-mode logic there can be combined with the allowlist gating from this one.

## Approach

Replaces the previous `try/catch` approach with the inspect-mode pattern already used in `extensions/firecrawl/src/config.ts`:

1. Calls `resolveSecretInputString` with `mode: "inspect"` so unresolved SecretRefs return `configured_unavailable` instead of throwing.
2. Treats `file` and `exec` SecretRefs as `blocked` — never falls through to ambient `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY`.
3. Treats env SecretRefs whose `id` is not `TAVILY_API_KEY` as `blocked` — same reason.
4. Validates the env provider allowlist via `canResolveEnvSecretRefInReadOnlyPath` before reading `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY`.
5. Trims whitespace from the configured id before matching (YAML config may pad env var names).
6. `resolveTavilyApiKey` only falls through to `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` when the configured SecretRef is `missing` (no apiKey configured) — never when it is `blocked`.

This addresses the ClawSweeper review feedback on the previous try/catch revision: the catch-all could silently route Tavily requests through ambient `TAVILY_API_KEY` when the user configured a different explicit SecretRef source (file, exec, or env with a different id), weakening the intended credential boundary.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — behavior change is limited to the previously-broken unresolvable-env-ref case; success path is identical.
- Config/env changes? **No**
- Migration needed? **No**
- CHANGELOG entry: **NOT included** in this PR, per `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("Maintainers or ClawSweeper add the changelog entry when landing user-facing changes"). ClawSweeper's 2026-06-19 review noted the previous manual entry to be removed; this revision drops it.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk:** a stricter upstream caller relies on the resolver throwing so it can surface the error to the user.
  - **Mitigation:** the only caller in this file (`resolveTavilyApiKey`) already has `process.env` and downstream-string fallbacks. The chain in `resolveTavilyApiKey` was always meant to handle an unresolvable ref; the throw was incidental.
- **Risk:** a future plugin re-introduces the same throw pattern.
  - **Mitigation:** the new tests in `extensions/tavily/src/config.test.ts` (3 inspect-mode positive paths, 5 negative paths, 8 cases total) assert the no-throw behavior, so any regression is caught at unit-test time.
- **Risk:** a future user configures a non-`TAVILY_API_KEY` env SecretRef (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY` for tavily) and the ambient `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` is silently used.
  - **Mitigation:** the new helper treats such refs as `blocked` and explicitly returns `undefined`; the test suite pins this behavior with dedicated cases.

* * *

## Generated with assistance from Aiko (AikoOpenClawBot), an AI agent running on OpenClaw 2026.6.10

- **Provider:** Kilo Gateway (`https://api.kilo.ai/api/gateway`)
- **Author:** Karol Zalewski [karol.zalewski@4zal.net](mailto:karol.zalewski@4zal.net)

target.title: fix(tui): keep assistant text chronological across tool calls and resume; condense tool cards
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two user-visible TUI rendering defects and one readability problem:

1. **Assistant text rendered out of chronological order around tool calls.** The TUI kept one streaming assistant component per run and updated it in place while tool cards appended separately, so text the model produced *after* a tool call rendered *above* that tool's card. The same defect corrupted ordering when replaying history on session resume.
2. **Tool cards were tall and noisy**, taking several lines each even when collapsed, which made runs with many tool calls hard to scan.
3. **With verbose mode off there was no indication of tool activity at all** — the TUI sat silent during long tool-heavy stretches.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Assistant streaming text is now segmented around tool cards: each new burst of assistant text after a tool call gets its own component in true arrival order, both live and on history replay (replay assigns distinct per-turn identities instead of merging a whole run into one block).
- Tool cards are condensed to one line with middle-ellipsis truncation.
- When verbose is off, a one-line tool-activity summary shows what the agent is doing instead of nothing.

Scope note: this PR originally also carried persistence for `!`/`!!` local shell commands; per review feedback it was split out and now lives in #103648. This PR is purely rendering/display.

## User Impact

- Assistant text and tool cards appear in the order they actually happened, live and after resume.
- Tool-heavy runs are much more compact and scannable.
- Verbose-off sessions show a lightweight activity line instead of appearing frozen.

## Evidence

- `src/tui/components/chat-log.test.ts` — regression tests for chronological segmentation live and on replay.
- `src/tui/tool-activity-summary.test.ts` — activity summary behavior.
- `src/tui/tui-event-handlers.test.ts`, `src/tui/tui-session-actions.test.ts` — event wiring and resume-ordering coverage.
- Full `src/tui` suite green locally; fake-backend PTY lane green (`test/vitest/vitest.tui-pty.config.ts`).
- **Real-terminal evidence** (real gateway, live inference, no mocks): live compact cards + chronological ordering, verbose-off summaries, and resume replay in both verbose tiers — https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103147#issuecomment-4975353033. The recording process itself surfaced two replay defects, both fixed in-branch with regression tests (see the comment).

target.title: fix(gateway): don't retire parent Codex binding when creating a detached dashboard child
target.body:
Fixes #106778

## What Problem This Solves

Creating a dashboard child from an active Codex-backed channel session (Control UI → new dashboard chat — an ordinary child creation, not a fork) succeeds but **retires the parent session's Codex binding**, even though the parent remains the channel's current session. The next inbound parent turn then fails permanently with `Codex binding generation was retired`, recoverable only by manual SQLite surgery.

Root-cause chain (all on current `main`):
1. `createGatewaySession` emits a terminal `session_end(reason:"new")` on the **parent** for any parent-linked child when `emitCommandHooks === true` — `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`.
2. The Codex extension treats `"new"` as terminal (`ENDED_SESSION_REASONS`) and its `session_end` handler calls `bindingStore.retireSessionGeneration()` — `extensions/codex/index.ts:48,274`.
3. The next lease attempt observes the retired generation and throws `Codex binding generation was retired`.

A detached dashboard child (its own `agent:<id>:dashboard:*` key) runs **in parallel** — it does not replace the parent as the channel's current session, so emitting a terminal `session_end` on the parent is wrong.

## Approach

The parent rolls over — terminal `session_end` on the parent, `session_start` on the child — only when the child **succeeds** it. That disposition cannot be inferred from the child's key shape: the server keeps no current-session pointer, so a key namespace cannot prove succession (the earlier `startsWith("dashboard:")` gate was a heuristic). The caller declares it explicitly via a new optional `succeedsParent` flag on `sessions.create`; the gate reads the flag:

```ts
const childSucceedsParent = params.fork !== true && params.succeedsParent === true;
```

The namespace invariant is enforced by a **loud boundary validation** rather than silent inference: `succeedsParent` requires an explicit non-dashboard successor key and conflicts with `fork`; a keyless/minted or dashboard-namespaced child (auto-managed, detached) is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`. A mis-declared succession therefore fails loudly instead of silently retiring a still-active parent's binding.

- **Only TUI `/new`** (an explicit `tui-*` successor) declares `succeedsParent: true` — it still emits the parent `session_end` + child `session_start`.
- **Every other create path** — minted dashboard child (webchat "new chat"), fork, catalog/work child — is parallel by default and unchanged: no parent `session_end`, child `session_start` fires.
- **Main reset-in-place** emits its own hooks via `performGatewaySessionReset` and returns earlier; a dashboard session is replaced via `sessions.reset` (which retires its binding in place), never a create-succession.
- The parent's `before_reset` / `command:new` hooks (documented Control UI behavior, #76957) are untouched.

This is behavior-preserving vs the previous revision — the only path that emitted parent `session_end` (explicit `tui-*` successor) still does — while removing the fragile key-shape heuristic from the decision. Because succession is now opt-in, any out-of-tree caller that relied on *implicit* succession via an explicit key runs parallel until it declares `succeedsParent` (the safe direction: a not-retired parent can still be reset; a wrongly-retired one is broken).

**Changed in this revision:** replaced the `startsWith("dashboard:")` key-shape gate with the caller-declared `succeedsParent` flag + a boundary validation — addressing the standing P1 that the emit decision should be an explicit disposition, not a key-shape inference.

**Maintainer note.** The contract question — which Control UI / TUI creations *replace* the selected parent vs run alongside it — is genuinely a maintainer decision (given the #78215 lifecycle provenance, likely @BunsDev). This PR implements the recommended "explicit disposition" shape and preserves today's dispositions; a different contract (an enum, a different default) is a small adjustment.

Scope note: sibling issue #105817 (rejected *oversized* fork retires parent binding) is a **separate** path — fork-size rejection returns before this emit block — and is not addressed here.

## Evidence

### Persisted-state consequence — proven in-boundary over a real store

The destructive step lives in the Codex extension, and its bundled suite already asserts it over a **real** `createCodexAppServerBindingStore`: `session_end(reason:"new")` retires the generation (`read() → undefined` — the `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` tombstone #106778 reports), while non-terminal reasons (`shutdown`, `restart`, `compaction`) leave it intact. So the persisted mutation is real and reason-selective — suppressing the parent `session_end` for a parallel child is exactly what keeps the binding alive.

### Gate A/B + validation (real gateway session-create path, deterministic)

`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` toggles only the disposition:

```
explicit tui-* successor (succeedsParent)        → parent session_end(reason:"new") + child session_start
minted dashboard child (default)                 → no parent session_end; child session_start
fork                                             → no parent session_end
succeedsParent + {dashboard-keyed|keyless|fork}  → INVALID_REQUEST (no hooks)
```

- **65** focused lifecycle tests (`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` + `server.sessions.create.test.ts`) + **147** TUI tests pass (Node 25.9.0).
- **Static**: `tsgo:core` / `tsgo:core:test` clean.
- **Preservation**: `extensions/codex/` unchanged — a genuine `session_end reason:"new"` still retires the binding.

A full Codex app-server E2E completing model turns needs OpenAI auth unavailable in CI, but the model turn is orthogonal to this fix — the fix is precisely about *not* retiring the parent, which the gate + the in-boundary retirement suite together establish.

## Tests

`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` (explicit `tui-*` successor with `succeedsParent` → parent `session_end` + child `session_start`; detached dashboard child → no parent `session_end`, child `session_start`; reset-in-place + `command:new`/`before_reset` unchanged; **new** — `succeedsParent` + dashboard-keyed child, keyless child, and fork each → `INVALID_REQUEST`), `server.sessions.create.test.ts` (selected-global dashboard child and fork → no parent `session_end`), `tui-command-handlers.test.ts` (`/new` declares `succeedsParent: true`).

target.title: fix: doctor should not treat loopback bind as network-accessible 0.0.0.0
target.body:
Closes #107425

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with `gateway.bind = "loopback"` would see a false doctor security warning that the Gateway was network-accessible on `0.0.0.0`, even when the Gateway was only listening on loopback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor security classified exposure from the resolved bind host alone. When loopback mode's host resolution fell back to `0.0.0.0`, that host was treated as network-accessible. The fix preserves the canonical loopback bind mode as local-only for exposure classification, while still warning on real LAN/custom/auto exposure paths. No config keys, defaults, or auth behavior change.

Follow-up from review: the test mock holder for `resolveGatewayBindHost` now uses the production parameter type (`GatewayBindMode | undefined`) so `check-test-types` accepts assigning the real resolver.

Fix quality: compatibility (loopback semantic contract only; real non-loopback binds still warn), performance (one bind-mode check), usability (removes false security alarm), security (does not weaken LAN/custom exposure warnings).

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor` / security warnings no longer treat an explicit loopback bind as network-accessible when host resolution falls back to `0.0.0.0`. Operators with loopback-only Gateways avoid a false CRITICAL/WARNING exposure line.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS arm64 (path-scoped static checks + focused Vitest + live doctor lint with loopback config and listener inspection).

```text
# Focused behavior tests (after mock typing fix)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-security.test.ts
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  34 passed (34)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-security.test.ts -t "does not treat loopback bind fallback"
# ✓ does not treat loopback bind fallback resolution as network-accessible
```

Red/green contrast for the new regression case (same harness, production line temporarily set to main vs this patch):

**Before (main classification):**
```text
FAIL  does not treat loopback bind fallback resolution as network-accessible
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
Received:
  "- CRITICAL: Gateway bound to \"loopback\" (0.0.0.0) without authentication.
  Anyone on your network (or internet if port-forwarded) can fully control your agent.
  ..."
```

**After (this patch):**
```text
✓ does not treat loopback bind fallback resolution as network-accessible
Tests  1 passed | 33 skipped
```

Mock typing (review finding): holder uses `GatewayBindMode | undefined` to match `resolveGatewayBindHost`, so assigning the production function type-checks under `check-test-types`.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Doctor security must not report `Gateway bound to "loopback" (0.0.0.0)` as network-accessible when the configured bind mode is loopback. This is the same classification path used by `openclaw doctor --lint` security (`core/doctor/security` → `noteSecurityWarnings`).
- Environment: local macOS arm64, PR head after mock typing fix, isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` with `gateway.bind = "loopback"` and a redacted token auth field.
- Listener inspection while a loopback process was bound:
  ```text
  COMMAND   PID       USER   FD   TYPE  ... NAME
  node    18421 ... TCP 127.0.0.1:18789 (LISTEN)
  ```
- Live CLI after fix (loopback config, non-interactive lint JSON), redacted:
  ```bash
  OPENCLAW_HOME=<isolated> node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --non-interactive --json
  ```
  Observed security findings (excerpt): plaintext-token hygiene only (`gateway.auth.token`). **No** `Gateway bound` / `network-accessible` finding for the loopback bind.
  ```text
  checkId=core/doctor/security severity=warning
    WARNING: openclaw.json contains plaintext secret-bearing config fields.
    Paths: gateway.auth.token
  gateway bound any? False
  network-accessible any? False
  ```
- Forced 0.0.0.0 fallback path (issue repro class): with bind mode loopback and host resolution forced to `0.0.0.0`, `noteSecurityWarnings` emits no `Gateway bound` / `network-accessible` note (Vitest regression above). Current-main contrast still fails that case (see Evidence red/green).
- Control check: lan bind without auth still warns (`warns when exposed without auth` passes). Existing loopback normal path and unset-bind-as-loopback cases still pass.
- What was not tested: long-running managed Gateway service under a host where `canBindToHost("127.0.0.1")` itself fails (true extreme resolver fallback outside the forced harness); LAN/custom live install matrix.

target.title: fix(cron): persist startup catch-up deferrals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102236. A startup overflow catch-up slot could be persisted to SQLite while its protection marker existed only in memory. Restarting again before that slot fired let maintenance advance the job to its next natural cron slot, silently losing the deferred run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral marker now lives on `CronJobState` as `pendingCatchupDeferral`, so the existing `state_json` persistence and rollback paths own the slot and marker together. The process-local Set and its parallel rollback bookkeeping are removed. Maintenance clears the persisted marker when the slot arrives, when no valid deferred slot remains, or when the job is disabled; execution also clears it after an outcome. Existing rows need no migration because an absent field means no pending deferral.

## User Impact

Overflow system-event cron jobs keep their staggered startup catch-up run across repeated gateway restarts instead of silently skipping to the next natural schedule. Unrelated stale future cron slots are still repaired normally.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite restart path: one service starts and persists an overflow deferral, a fresh service starts 3 seconds later against the same store, the original 5-second slot survives, executes once, and clears its marker.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.startup-overflow-clobber.test.ts src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts src/cron/service/ops.test.ts`: 3 files, 107 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.restart-catchup.test.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts`: 2 files, 81 tests passed.
- Oxlint passed for all nine changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (74 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof
Temp root: /tmp/proof-101442-24382397-303b-4df6-9e58-5fb8b44c202a

  Normal file read ... OK: decoded="Hello from PR #101442.\n"
  Oversized file rejects ... OK: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442/huge.md
  Directory rejects as non-regular ... OK: path must be a regular file
  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop
```
The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/link-b.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 94342b49-9153-4f1a-bc8f-fa3a0ccbbb44 ended with stopReason=stop
```
The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

target.title: fix(wechat): preserve existing accounts across hot reload
target.body:
## Summary
- preserve known live accounts when an already-active channel hot-reload restarts without an explicit account id
- preserve known accounts for channel account-index reload markers such as `channels.openclaw-weixin.channelConfigUpdatedAt`
- avoid unioning stale manager-known accounts when a plugin channel was inactive before the same reload and becomes active afterward
- keep ordinary channel config reloads from resurrecting removed or disabled configured accounts
- treat hot-reload stop/restart as a manager-owned handoff only for channels that stayed active across plugin replacement
- document the WeChat multi-account behavior and cover the hot-reload paths with regression tests
- add a guard that ordinary caller-owned restarts still do not resurrect stale accounts
- harden the non-isolated agent model-catalog visibility coverage that timed out in refreshed CI

## Why
Adding a second WeChat account can temporarily surface only the new account in the plugin account listing. Before this change, the gateway could evict or fail to restart the already-running account during hot reload, leaving account A offline after account B logs in.

The latest repair covers the non-plugin account-index reload path called out by review: when a channel updates `channelConfigUpdatedAt`, the restart now includes manager-known accounts. The stale-account guard remains narrow because ordinary channel config edits still restart with the configured channel set only.

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles
- `config:docs:gen`/`check` clean; generated config reference updated


### Current-head proof (SHA `368c1f48d14f8b1d0cf0378d227c9d8e639787af`)

target.title: feat: add standard hosting profiles
target.body:
Related RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/37

Depends on: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104018

> **Stacked draft:** this branch contains exact readiness head `89d8607aab9f` from PR 104018 followed by seven profile-only commits. Until PR 104018 lands, GitHub's aggregate diff against `main` includes both layers. After it lands, this PR reduces to the Hosting Profiles work described below.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw runs locally, in containers, behind identity proxies, and as a controller for paired execution targets, but those deployment labels are not reproducible support contracts. Operators currently spread the intended posture across startup flags, environment, config, container probes, adapter code, and private checklists. A Gateway process can be alive and logging while it still cannot safely serve its intended workload.

This change makes that distinction explicit. A selected profile names the posture OpenClaw is expected to satisfy, and the canonical readiness result remains `503` with stable reasons until every required runtime fact is true.

## Standard Hosting Profiles

Profiles are named, release-tested presets over the canonical readiness conditions from PR 104018. They do not introduce a second health system.

| Profile | Supported posture | Additional required readiness evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `local` | Default foreground or local Gateway | Universal Gateway readiness and writable workspace |
| `container` | Directly reachable container listener | Non-loopback effective listener and writable mounted workspace |
| `reverse-proxy` | Gateway behind a trusted identity proxy | Trusted-proxy auth mode, identity header, trusted source, and writable workspace |
| `node-mode` | Gateway controlling one or more execution targets | Approved pairing, connected target, approved command surface, live control channel, and writable workspace |

Selection is optional and resolves in this order:

```text
gateway startup argument > environment > openclaw.json > local default
```

Operators select a profile through `hosting.profile`, `OPENCLAW_HOSTING_PROFILE`, or `gateway run --hosting-profile`. Invalid startup values fail before destructive runtime reset/force behavior. Results include a logical runtime ID and a unique process/container incarnation ID.

Profiles validate effective runtime state. They do not generate or repair configuration, encode scheduler retry policy, introduce Lobster/OCC concepts, or replace direct readiness-condition selection.

## Why This Helps Operators

Docker, Kubernetes, systemd, OCC, and downstream hosts can consume the ordinary `/readyz` contract instead of reconstructing readiness from logs or process liveness. A host receives `200` only when the selected posture can serve work; expected deployment failures return `503` and a named condition explaining what remains unmet.

This matters most for partial startup. For example, node-mode remains non-ready when its Gateway is running, and remains non-ready even after a node transport connects, until the node command surface is explicitly approved. The host does not send traffic merely because a process exists.

Maintainers gain a bounded support matrix for reproducing deployment issues against a named posture rather than an open-ended configuration claim.

## Implementation Stack

Readiness dependency head: `89d8607aab9f`

Profile-only commits:

1. `44c0f163489` standard `local`, `container`, and `reverse-proxy` profiles
2. `d1a47217be6` product-neutral `node-mode` readiness
3. `057ad938451` runtime activation identity
4. `ee942d3989a` packaged profile conformance and release wiring
5. `02602feb858` startup validation and lifecycle safety
6. `1448fb9c749` host-provisioned workspace proof
7. `a416b9b9192` explicit node approval readiness proof

Profile-only diff: 32 files, 1,330 insertions, and 5 deletions, including docs and tests. `git range-diff` reports every profile commit patch-identical to the previously reviewed stack.

Fork review slices: [#18](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/18), [#19](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/19), [#42](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/42), and [#21](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/21). [Fork PR #94](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/94) preserves the profile-only diff against the readiness branch.

## Verification

Exact source head: `a416b9b9192b55ed2be54ad1124c2bbf7b632d9a`

Environment: isolated Ubuntu 24.04 checkout, Node 24.15+, Docker Linux/amd64. No Lobster, OCC, tenant service, or unpublished local dependency was involved.

Focused source verification:

- 310 assertions passed across the changed profile, runtime, node-mode, config, CLI, planner, release, Gateway startup, and readiness files.
- The one profile-added `gateway.test.ts` startup assertion also passes alone. Two unrelated cases in that broad file fail identically on the exact readiness base (`sessions.abort` timeout and workspace-plugin registration count), so they are recorded as inherited base failures rather than profile regressions.
- Shell syntax, JavaScript syntax, Oxfmt on 30 files, Oxlint on 26 files, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Codex review of the seven profile-only commits against readiness head `89d8607aab9f` found no actionable correctness regression.

Package-installed Docker verification:

```text

  bash scripts/e2e/hosting-profiles-docker.sh
```

The exact-head run exited `0`, built the package and functional Docker image, reported `OpenClaw package tarball integrity passed`, and completed with `Hosting profiles Docker E2E passed`.

Image: `sha256:e87c9e0651d60b6b58262b6ee271f89d0bee060fd2761d0da1525aca60fd6337`

target.title: fix(slack): mark connected status degraded without bot identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Slack `auth.test` fails at boot, or `channels.slack.botToken` is actually a user token (`xoxp` with `user_id` but no `bot_id`), Socket Mode can still connect while main previously published `healthState: "healthy"`. Operators see a connected channel while mention detection is disabled and required-mention rooms fail closed — silent inbound loss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transport liveness (`connected: true`) remains useful, but advertising `healthy` is wrong when bot identity is missing under the current bot_id-gated contract (`botUserId = botId ? authUserId : ""`). Publish `healthState: "degraded"` with `lastError`, and log `slack socket mode connected (degraded identity)`.

## User Impact

- Misconfigured bot tokens / failed `auth.test` no longer look healthy in channel status.
- Valid bot-token installs stay `healthy` on connect.
- App Home slash-command wiring and allowlist-resolution formatting are untouched.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

## What Problem This Solves

Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading, caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, block the loop for 14-22 seconds and drop messages (issue #87509 reports 14-22s bootstrap-context stalls that block channel I/O, WebSocket keepalive, and timers).

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

## Why This Change Was Made

Bootstrap extra-file loading runs during embedded-run bootstrap-context, on the hot path that prepares every agent turn. On `main` the exported loader reaches Node `fs.glob` and synchronous fd reads, which monopolize the event loop over a large workspace; this change routes the same exported loader through an async yielding walker and async fd reads, and yields between bootstrap hook handlers, so channel I/O stays responsive during bootstrap. The public plugin SDK surface is deliberately unchanged.

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

## User Impact

Agents whose workspaces contain large trees or broad `bootstrap-extra-files` globs no longer stall the event loop for seconds during bootstrap-context, so WebSocket keepalives, typing indicators, HTTP requests, and timers keep firing while an agent turn is being prepared — messages are no longer dropped. The set of bootstrap files loaded is unchanged (identical glob match set), so no agent sees different context. Root bootstrap file loading goes serial-sync → parallel-async, glob walks go blocking → yielding, and hook chains go uninterrupted → yielded.

## Evidence

This is a **current-`main` vs current-PR-head** real-behavior benchmark against the real exported loader, covering elapsed time, event-loop responsiveness, glob-match parity, and RSS.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces (issue #87509). This change replaces the native `fs.glob` walk with an async walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries so the event loop stays responsive, while returning the identical configured `bootstrap-extra-files` match set.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. `main` = `9b823c610816` (native `fs.glob`, synchronous fd reads); head = `3dfd7f1d4952` (async yielding walker, async fd reads). The identical benchmark script runs inside each checkout (relative import binds to that checkout's implementation); both consume the same pre-built read-only workspace.
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of **395,807 filesystem entries** (391,124 files, 4,683 dirs — wide flat dirs + a deep 40-level tree + `node_modules` + `.git` + `.hidden` noise), with `AGENTS.md` planted at several depths (root, deep-past-old-cutoff, `.hidden/`, `node_modules/`). Configured pattern `**/AGENTS.md`. During the load a 5ms repeating timer counts liveness ticks, `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay({resolution:5})` records event-loop delay, and `process.memoryUsage().rss` is captured before/after with `global.gc()`. 3 fresh processes per side after a discarded warmup; values below are medians.
- **Failing proof before fix** (current `main` `9b823c610816`, native `fs.glob`):
  ```
  elapsed: 834.5ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 55.5ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 8.50ms   p99: 54.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 95 / 166 expected (57.2% kept)
  rssDelta: 358.3 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: fs.glob finishes the walk fast but monopolizes the loop —
          multi-tens-of-ms stalls, ~43% of 5ms liveness ticks dropped, 358 MB RSS spike
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch** (identical script both sides; full reproduce recipe below):
  ```
  # build the shared 395,807-entry workspace once, then run each side from its own checkout
  node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws"
  ```
- **Evidence after fix** (current PR head `3dfd7f1d4952`, async yielding walker):
  ```
  elapsed: 1244.8ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 10.7ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 5.09ms   p99: 6.6ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 245 / 248 expected (98.8% kept)
  rssDelta: 57.0 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: yielding walker keeps the loop responsive — max delay near the 5ms floor,
          98.8% of liveness ticks fired, RSS footprint ~6x smaller
  ```
- **Glob result parity (main vs head)**: sha256 of the sorted relative match set is **identical** on both sides — `b90d55afa71f2aa871ea40de7d91715377c93b76d26e7f43d817019b6b72a97e`. Matched set both sides: `AGENTS.md`, the deep 40-level `deep/.../AGENTS.md`, and `node_modules/pkg000/AGENTS.md`; `.git` and `.hidden/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded by both. The custom walker changes event-loop behavior and memory, not the returned file set.

  | metric (median of 3, 395,807 entries, Node v24.10.0) | main `9b823c610816` | head `3dfd7f1d4952` |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | elapsed (ms) | 834.5 | 1244.8 |
  | max event-loop delay (ms) | 55.5 | 10.7 |
  | mean event-loop delay (ms) | 8.50 | 5.09 |
  | liveness ticks kept | 57.2% | 98.8% |
  | RSS delta (MB) | 358.3 | 57.0 |
  | `**/AGENTS.md` matches returned | 3 | 3 (identical set) |

- **Observed result after fix**: the fix trades a modest wall-clock increase (834ms → 1245ms) for the property the issue actually needs — the event loop stops stalling. Max event-loop delay drops from 55.5ms to 10.7ms (near the 5ms probe floor), liveness-tick retention rises from 57.2% to 98.8%, and peak RSS is ~6x smaller (358MB → 57MB) because the walker no longer buffers the whole `fs.glob` result eagerly. The returned match set is byte-identical (same sha256), so existing `bootstrap-extra-files` configs load the same files. At the field-report scale (much larger real workspaces), `main`'s blocking walk is what produces the 14-22s embedded_run stalls; this benchmark demonstrates the direction and mechanism (blocking `fs.glob` vs cooperative yielding) at 395,807 entries on a single dev box.
- **Reproduce**:
  ```bash
  BENCH=/tmp/bench-89040
  PR=<pr-head-checkout>
  git -C "$PR" worktree add --detach "$BENCH/main-wt" 9b823c610816   # current upstream/main
  ln -s "$PR/node_modules" "$BENCH/main-wt/node_modules"             # read-only bench, first-party deps
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$PR/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$BENCH/main-wt/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  # build the shared workspace once (reused by both sides, walk mutates nothing)
  (cd "$PR" && node --import tsx/esm "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" build "$BENCH/ws" 400000)
  # 3 fresh processes per side, run from inside each checkout so the relative import binds
  (cd "$PR"            && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  (cd "$BENCH/main-wt" && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  ```
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real exported glob-resolution path (`loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics`) and event-loop instrumentation directly rather than through a connected channel. The main-side `node_modules` is symlinked from the head checkout, which is valid because `workspace.ts`'s transitive imports are first-party and the run is read-only. Focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: fix: reconcile config watcher after recreation
target.body:
Related: #103729

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators editing the gateway configuration while its file watcher is recovering from an error can have those edits silently ignored. A replacement Chokidar watcher may absorb changes made during downtime into its initial baseline without emitting an `add`, `change`, or `unlink` event.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replacement watchers now perform one reconciliation read after their initial `ready` scan. The initial startup watcher remains quiet, preserving existing startup behavior, while both native watcher recreation and polling fallback cover edits made during recovery.

## User Impact

Gateway configuration edits made while the watcher is being recreated are applied after recovery instead of remaining unapplied until a later filesystem event or restart.

## Evidence

- Added regression coverage for replacement native watchers and polling fallback watchers.
- Verified the tests red before the implementation: 2 new tests failed because no snapshot was read after replacement watcher readiness.
- Verified the implementation before the latest `main` sync with `pnpm test src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts`: 134 tests passed.
- Verified the merged contribution diff with `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.
- GitHub CI on commit `a4f6a50a`: 68 successful checks and zero failures, including all Node test shards, lint, type checks, artifact build, smoke tests, CodeQL, OpenGrep, and Real behavior proof.
